Metadata.title: Galopen
Metadata.description: A macOS menu bar app that shows your calendar events and auto-opens meeting URLs.

Hero.description: Galopen lives in your macOS menu bar, showing upcoming calendar events and automatically opening meeting URLs right when you need them.

Why.title: Erase the "where's the meeting link" shuffle.
Why.description: Notification fires → switch to calendar → find the event → copy the URL → paste into the browser. A few seconds, every time — and on days with back-to-back Zoom / Meet / Teams calls, those seconds turn into "sorry I'm late." Galopen removes the whole routine.

Services.title: Works with
Services.description: Detects meeting URLs from any calendar already synced to your Mac.

menuBar.title: Menu Bar Native
menuBar.description: Lives quietly in your menu bar. Click to see today's and tomorrow's schedule at a glance.

autoOpen.title: Auto-Open Meetings
autoOpen.description: Automatically opens Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams links at a configurable time before the meeting starts.

countdown.title: Countdown Timer
countdown.description: See how many minutes until your next meeting, right in the menu bar. Configurable display threshold.

calendars.title: Calendar Filtering
calendars.description: Toggle visibility of individual calendars. Works with all calendars synced to your Mac.

privacy.title: Privacy First
privacy.description: All data stays on your Mac. No accounts, no servers, no tracking. Uses the native macOS EventKit.

lightweight.title: Lightweight
lightweight.description: Built with Tauri for minimal resource usage. Small download, fast startup, low memory footprint.

CTA.title: Get started in seconds.
CTA.description: Download Galopen, grant calendar access, and you're good to go. Free and open source.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: Galopen reads your calendar so it can open the right meeting at the right time. That's personal information, so here is where it goes: nowhere. There is no server behind this app, no analytics, and no account to sign into.

sections.title: It reads the calendar already on your Mac
sections.body: Galopen asks macOS for your events through the system calendar, which is why it prompts for calendar access on first launch. It does not connect to Google, Microsoft, or anyone else, and there is no login. Whatever calendars your Mac already has are the calendars it sees.

sections.title: Your events stay on the Mac
sections.body: Event titles, times, and meeting links are used to show today's schedule and to open the right URL when a meeting starts. None of it is uploaded, logged to a server, or shared. There is nowhere for it to go.

sections.title: Opening a meeting
sections.body: When Galopen opens a meeting, it hands the URL to your browser and stops there. What happens after that is between you and Zoom, Meet, Teams, or whoever is hosting — their own privacy policies apply, the same as if you had clicked the link yourself.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: The app checks for new versions by fetching a small file from its GitHub Releases page. GitHub sees the request the way it sees any download, including your IP address. Nothing about your calendar is included.

sections.title: No analytics, ever
sections.body: There is no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no unique identifier, and no third-party SDK of any kind in the app.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Galopen is open source under the MIT license, so none of the above has to be taken on trust. Read the source, or open an issue if something looks wrong.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version starts doing something new with your data, this page gets updated before that version ships.
